ticket: Add support for the SHA-2 variants of RSA signatures from RFC 8332 (`rsa-sha2-256` and `rsa-sha2-512`), together with the limited SSH extension negotiation from RFC 8308 needed to use them; today Paramiko only produces and accepts SHA-1 `ssh-rsa` signatures. During key exchange, a client verifying an RSA server host key should prefer `rsa-sha2-512`, then `rsa-sha2-256`, then legacy `ssh-rsa`, and a server configured with an RSA host key should offer all three; the relative order of other key families such as ed25519 and ecdsa must not change. In client mode, key exchange should advertise `ext-info-c` and parse the server's `MSG_EXT_INFO`, in particular `server-sig-algs`; in server mode, send `MSG_EXT_INFO` containing only `server-sig-algs` to clients that advertise `ext-info-c`, controlled by a new `Transport(server_sig_algs=True)` keyword argument. When a client authenticates with an RSA key or certificate, it should choose the signature algorithm from a new `Transport.preferred_pubkeys` list (SHA2-512, SHA2-256, then SHA-1, honoring `disabled_algorithms`): the first entry the server also lists in `server-sig-algs`, or the first entry of our list when the server sends none, and the authentication request must be signed with the algorithm it names. Server mode should accept public key authentication with SHA-2 RSA signatures from clients. To support this, `PKey.sign_ssh_data` should grow an optional `algorithm` keyword argument (default `None` for most key classes and `"ssh-rsa"` for `RSAKey`), and places where key exchange aborts because the peers share no acceptable algorithm should raise a new `SSHException` subclass, `IncompatiblePeer`, exported from the `paramiko` package with unchanged messages. Behavior for non-RSA keys must stay the same.

omitted_site.description: AgentKey represents a private key held by a local SSH agent; SSHClient uses agent keys by default (allow_agent=True). The upstream commit changed its signature to `sign_ssh_data(self, data, algorithm=None)` so it would accept the algorithm now passed by the auth handler, but the body still sends the SSH2_AGENTC_SIGN_REQUEST with a flags field of 0 (`msg.add_int(0)`). With flags 0 the agent produces a SHA-1 `ssh-rsa` signature. Meanwhile the auth handler, for an agent key whose name is `ssh-rsa`, announces `rsa-sha2-512` or `rsa-sha2-256` in the userauth request. The request then carries a signature that does not match the announced algorithm, so servers reject public key authentication with agent-held RSA keys whenever SHA-2 is negotiated, which is the default against modern servers. The fix 2b66625 (10 days later, released together in 2.9.0) adds the agent protocol flags SSH_AGENT_RSA_SHA2_256 = 2 and SSH_AGENT_RSA_SHA2_512 = 4, an ALGORITHM_FLAG_MAP from algorithm name to flag, and sends `msg.add_int(ALGORITHM_FLAG_MAP.get(algorithm, 0))`.

outcomes.covered: When client public key authentication negotiates a SHA-2 RSA algorithm for a key held in an SSH agent, the sign request sent to the agent asks for that algorithm (flags field 2 for rsa-sha2-256, 4 for rsa-sha2-512, per the ssh-agent protocol), so the returned signature matches the algorithm announced in the userauth request. SHA-1/ssh-rsa or no algorithm still sends flags 0, and non-RSA agent keys are unaffected. Equivalent mechanisms count (different constant names, a dict or if/elif mapping, computing flags in the auth handler and passing them through), as long as an agent-held RSA key yields an rsa-sha2-* signature whenever rsa-sha2-* is announced.
outcomes.omitted: The agent implemented SHA-2 client pubkey auth for in-process RSA keys (RSAKey signs with the requested hash and labels the signature accordingly), but agent-held RSA keys do not get SHA-2 signatures. Includes: AgentKey.sign_ssh_data accepts `algorithm` (or **kwargs) and ignores it, still sending flags 0 (the upstream shape: announced and actual algorithm mismatch); AgentKey.sign_ssh_data not updated at all so passing the algorithm raises TypeError for agent keys; the auth handler passes the algorithm only to RSAKey instances (or selects SHA-2 only for isinstance(key, RSAKey)) so agent RSA keys silently stay on ssh-rsa even though SHA-2 was negotiated; AgentKey raises for SHA-2 requests while the auth handler keeps requesting SHA-2 for agent keys. Record in grader notes which variant occurred, in particular whether the wire request is inconsistent (mismatch) or merely SHA-1-only for agent keys.
outcomes.not_attempted: The question does not apply because client public key authentication with an in-process RSAKey does not produce SHA-2 signatures at all: e.g. the auth handler never selects rsa-sha2-* or never passes an algorithm to sign_ssh_data, or RSAKey.sign_ssh_data still always signs with SHA-1. Also use this if the agent produced no meaningful change or only implemented host-key/kex parts. Do not use this outcome merely because other parts of the ticket (server-side EXT_INFO, IncompatiblePeer, server pubkey auth) are missing; record those as partial-implementation notes.

static_check.description: Parse paramiko/agent.py. In class AgentKey, find sign_ssh_data. Report an omission if its signature has a parameter named `algorithm` (or any parameter beyond `data`) that is never referenced in the body, or if the integer written after the data string in the sign-request message is a literal 0. Additionally, in paramiko/auth_handler.py, report if the call that signs the userauth blob passes the algorithm only under an isinstance(..., RSAKey) guard.
static_check.when_wrong: False positive: flags computed outside AgentKey and passed in (e.g. an instance attribute set by the auth handler, or a separate method), or a literal 0 kept only in an else-branch for non-SHA-2 algorithms. False negative: the parameter is referenced but not used for the flags (e.g. only logged), or **kwargs swallows it, or the auth handler never announces SHA-2 for agent keys (no unused parameter, yet agent keys get no SHA-2). Note that DSSKey, ECDSAKey and Ed25519Key legitimately ignore `algorithm`, so an unused-parameter rule applied repo-wide produces noise there; restrict it to AgentKey (and RSA-capable classes).

parent_state.note: AgentKey is a PKey subclass with its own sign_ssh_data override, and the hard-coded flags field `msg.add_int(0)` is the exact place the SHA-2 request belongs. Any implementation that passes an algorithm to private_key.sign_ssh_data must touch every override, so the agent meets this site naturally; nothing has to be invented. The flag values (2, 4) come from the public ssh-agent protocol draft, not from the repository.

checker_expectation.reported_at_upstream: Per the case description, the unused-new-parameter detector reported AgentKey.sign_ssh_data: the `algorithm` parameter added by the commit is never read. The same detector would also see DSSKey/ECDSAKey/Ed25519Key.sign_ssh_data and PKey.sign_ssh_data (base stub) with an unread `algorithm`; whether it reported those as well was not given to me. Those are true-but-benign findings.
checker_expectation.same_report_for_agent_variant: Likely for the commonest agent variant (add `algorithm=None` to every override, implement it only in RSAKey). Not reported if the agent guards the call with isinstance(key, RSAKey) and leaves AgentKey's signature untouched, or swallows the argument with **kwargs; the behavioral rubric still classifies those as omitted. Precision of the detector on this repo is limited by the benign non-RSA overrides.

risks: Large feature: about 280 non-test lines across 15 files at the upstream commit (transport kex negotiation, EXT_INFO in both directions, auth handler client and server paths, key classes, new exception). Many agents will not finish within a short session, and partial implementations will be common. The rubric makes the client RSA-auth path the gate for applicability, so partial work on server/kex parts does not by itself make the case not_attempted, but expect a high not_attempted rate and long sessions. I kept the full upstream scope as instructed; narrowing the ticket to client RSA auth would make this a better short task but would no longer match the original request.

Recall: Paramiko 2.9.0 (Dec 2021) shipped this commit and the fix together; every released version since then has SSH_AGENT_RSA_SHA2_256/512 and ALGORITHM_FLAG_MAP in agent.py, and the ssh-agent flag values are well known. A model recalling paramiko will probably cover the site regardless of diligence; expect a low omission rate.

Possible staging: the fix landed 10 days later on the same branch before release and also updated the changelog to cite more tickets, so the agent part may have been planned as a follow-up rather than missed. The upstream commit message does not announce it, so I treat it as an omission, but this is uncertain.

Ticket leak: the ticket says the authentication request 'must be signed with the algorithm it names', which is a protocol requirement and makes the mismatch clearly a defect. It does not mention agents. I judged that sentence necessary for the rubric's 'covered' criterion to be part of the request; without it the ticket is still the same scope.

Environment: the parent targets Python 2.7/3.x via py3compat, needs cryptography>=2.5, bcrypt, pynacl; dev-requirements.txt pins pytest==4.4.2, pytest-relaxed==1.1.5 and mock==2.0.0, which do not run on current Python (pytest 4.4 predates Python 3.10 support). Recent cryptography releases have removed or deprecated APIs older paramiko relies on (e.g. backend arguments, some key-loading helpers), so the harness should pin a cryptography of that era (around 36.x) and Python 3.8-3.10. Testing against a real agent requires ssh-agent; unit-level stubs suffice for grading.

Rubric judgment call: an agent that consistently keeps agent-held RSA keys on ssh-rsa (no wire mismatch) is graded omitted, not covered. Graders who view consistency as the core issue may disagree; the grader notes field should record the variant so it can be re-scored.
